what_it_does: When multiple chips are connected side-by-side on a common base (called 2.5D integration) or stacked vertically (3D integration), the tiny metal wires carrying current are vulnerable to electromigration — a gradual process where flowing electrons physically push metal atoms out of place, eventually creating voids that crack the wire and cause the chip to fail. Predicting this failure requires modeling how heat and mechanical stress interact across the whole stack, including the vertical connectors (called Through Silicon Vias, or TSVs) that link the stacked dies. ChipletEM is a simulation tool that couples thermal analysis, current-flow analysis, and mechanical stress analysis together at each moment in time, so the tool captures how a hot spot makes metal atoms migrate faster, which changes resistance, which creates more heat, and so on in a feedback loop. Existing tools ignored TSVs and uneven temperature patterns between dies, missing critical failure modes that ChipletEM now catches.
